body:
Hi, I'm the Playwright bot and I took a first look at this.

**Reproduced on tip-of-tree (npm `1.64.0-alpha-2026-09-15`, Firefox 155.0 build 1544), on Windows** — same platform you reported. Your script gave **7 stuck `goto`s out of 200** with the COOP header, **0 of 200** without it, and **0 of 200** with `browser.tabs.remote.useCrossOriginOpenerPolicy: false`. That matches your numbers, and your read of the cause matches the code: the content-side channel uid is `'process-' + Services.appinfo.processID` ([juggler/content/main.js#L64](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/main/browser_patches/firefox/juggler/content/main.js#L64)), while `SimpleChannel` only clears `_bufferedResponses` when the peer uid changes ([SimpleChannel.js#L173](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/main/browser_patches/firefox/juggler/SimpleChannel.js#L173)) — so a same-process browsing-context replacement gets a fresh channel with restarting request ids and a stale response cache. Real bug, Firefox-only by construction.

<details>
<summary>What I ran</summary>

- OS: Windows (GitHub Actions `windows-latest`), Node 24.20.0
- Playwright: `playwright@next` → `1.64.0-alpha-2026-09-15`, Firefox 155.0 (build 1544), headless
- Your `repro.mjs` verbatim, 4 workers, 200 trials, 10s `goto` timeout:

| run | stuck / trials |
| --- | --- |
| `node repro.mjs coop 200` | **7 / 200** |
| `node repro.mjs none 200` | 0 / 200 |
| `coop 200` + `firefoxUserPrefs: { 'browser.tabs.remote.useCrossOriginOpenerPolicy': false }` | 0 / 200 |

Not run across chromium/webkit: the failure is in the Firefox-specific juggler channel, and both other engines use different transports entirely.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Why the response cache is the suspect</summary>

`SimpleChannel._onMessage` clears `_bufferedResponses` only on a uid change during the `READY` / `READY_ACK` handshake. With `fission.webContentIsolationStrategy = 0`, the COOP-triggered browsing-context replacement stays in the same content process, so the new channel presents the same `'process-<pid>'` uid while its `_messageId` counter restarts at 1. Any not-yet-`RESPONSE_ACK`ed entry from the old channel then answers the new channel's message with the matching requestId, and that message — usually `Page.navigationCommitted` in these runs — is never delivered. That's consistent with what you see: the page is loaded, `waitForLoadState('load')` returns immediately, and a second `goto` unblocks it.
</details>

Two things that would help a maintainer picking this up: a uid derived per channel instance (rather than per process) is the shape you suggested, and it'd want checking against the cross-process swap path that `_bufferedResponses` exists to protect. Also worth noting this is likely the same root cause as #42183.

Thanks for the unusually thorough writeup — the pref toggle and the COEP comparison made this quick to confirm.


<sub>Triaged on Windows by the Playwright bot - [agent run](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/actions/runs/35036666902)</sub>

body:
I've confirmed the mechanism against a patched build and have a one-line fix. Numbers and evidence below.

### The collision, captured

I instrumented the `_bufferedResponses` hit path and the two handshake sites in a locally patched Firefox and ran the repro 200 times with the COOP header.

Every stuck navigation came with a cache hit whose cached response belonged to a *different* method than the incoming request — 44 mismatched hits against 44 hangs, one for one:

```
JUGGLER_CACHEHIT {"uid":"target-49b1bc86-…","connectedToUID":"process-59164",
 "requestId":12,"incomingMethod":"pageNavigationCommitted","incomingNamespace":"page",
 "cachedMethod":"pageNavigationStarted","mismatch":true}
```

All 44 were identical in shape: `requestId=12`, incoming `pageNavigationCommitted`, cached `pageNavigationStarted`. The committed event is the one `goto` is waiting for, which is why the page is fully loaded while the promise never settles.

The handshake log shows why the cache survived:

```
JUGGLER_READY {"uid":"target-44f09a36-…","wasConnectedTo":"process-72640",
 "nowConnectedTo":"process-72640","cleared":false,"cacheSize":0}
```

A COOP mismatch replaces the browsing context but `fission.webContentIsolationStrategy = 0` keeps it in the same content process, so the new `SimpleChannel` presents the same `'process-<pid>'` uid while its `_messageId` restarts at 1. `cleared:false`, and the previous channel's un-acked responses answer the new channel's opening request ids.

One browser-side channel saw **200 distinct content uids across 200 trials** — exactly one collision per trial.

### The fix

`browser_patches/firefox/juggler/content/main.js`:

```diff
-  data.channel = new SimpleChannel('', 'process-' + Services.appinfo.processID);
+  data.channel = new SimpleChannel('', 'process-' + Services.appinfo.processID + '-' + helper.generateId());
```

`helper` is already in scope and `generateId()` returns a UUID. Nothing in `SimpleChannel.js` changes — the comparison logic is already correct, only its input was wrong. The header there already says two instances on the same end must not share an id; `'process-' + pid` breaks that as soon as one process holds two top-level browsing contexts for a target.

I originally suggested keying on the browsing context id. I'd now argue against it: if the old actor's `didDestroy` runs before the new actor's `actorCreated`, the map entry is gone and the next channel carries the same context id, so the collision returns. The collision is per channel instance, and `initialize()` is where the instance is constructed.

### Measurements

200 trials per arm, the script from the issue, unmodified. The two COOP arms ran back to back in one session, patched first, so the zero isn't a quiet machine.

| Build | Mode | `goto` timeouts |
|---|---|---|
| Patched | COOP | **0 / 200** |
| Unpatched | COOP | **50 / 200** |
| Patched | no COOP | 0 / 200 |
| Unpatched | no COOP | 0 / 200 |

Across the session the unpatched build failed 44, 43 and 50 of 200 on three separate COOP runs; patched was 0 of 200 twice.

### The double-dispatch risk

The obvious hazard is the inverse of the bug — clearing the cache more often could let a re-sent request be handled twice, which is what `_bufferedResponses` exists to prevent. Same workload, instrumented:

| | Cache hits | Mismatched | Hangs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unpatched, COOP | 1,844 | 44 | 44 |
| Patched, COOP | 1,800 | 0 | 0 |

It removes exactly the 44 bad hits and keeps all 1,800 good ones, which is what I'd expect if the protected case is same-instance-new-transport: an instance's uid is fixed at construction, so the fix can't affect it.

Plain and cross-origin navigation never touch the cache at all in this repro (0 hits in 200 trials, both builds), so those arms prove nothing on their own. COOP+COEP does force a real cross-process swap and does exercise it: 3,355 hits unpatched against 3,190 patched, 0 mismatched and 0 hangs either way.

I also counted protocol-visible events across 400 navigations per build in each mode — frame navigations, loads, and document content — and they're identical between builds.

### What I haven't done

- **Not built from source.** I patched the juggler files inside `omni.ja` in the prebuilt Firefox and ran against that, which is what `browser_patches/repack-juggler.mjs` used to do before the infra move. The change would need to go in the source tree properly.
- **No Playwright test suite run** — only the repro and my own navigation counts. My double-dispatch check watches three signals, so a duplicate of some other protocol message wouldn't show up in it.
- **One machine, one build.** Windows 11, Firefox 155.0 build 1543, Playwright 1.63.0.
- **0/200 isn't absence.** A rarer residual race would survive this sample.
- I'm **not** claiming this fixes #42183. That reporter's app sets no COOP and their failures aren't first-navigation-only, so a shared cause is a guess, not something I've shown.


### One related thing

`WorkerMain.js:11` constructs `new SimpleChannel('worker::content', 'unique_identifier')` with a hardcoded literal uid, which looks like the same class of problem if two worker channels are ever live on one end. I haven't investigated or touched it.
